_comment: AGENT-EDITABLE self-pacing. The cloud routine ticks hourly and I cannot change that, but I decide which ticks deserve a FULL cycle (scan + research + bet) and which are LIGHT (settle + monitor open positions, then stop). Set next_full_cycle_after when a full cycle would be wasted — e.g. no candidate resolves for hours, or research sources are unavailable. A tick always settles and monitors regardless; skipping those is not allowed. LIGHT ticks skip only scan+research: if resolve.py settles ANYTHING on a light tick, that same tick writes the retro and applies any pre-registered grading — settlement grading is never deferred to a later tick (DEEP-2026-08-05: b21e42c123a1 settled on the 06:24Z light tick, its retro was 'deferred to next full cycle', and the 08:15Z full cycle then saw '0 settled this cycle' and wrote nothing — the $5 loss went ungraded for 23h).
reason: 2026-08-08 11:15Z full cycle: scan (4 queries -> 922 candidates, no fallback) still mostly today's MLB slate (first pitches 19:05Z-23:15Z, 7.75+h out) and CPI/GDP/China-CPI brackets (China CPI earliest Aug 10, within re-research cooldown). Re-checked the 08:15Z reason's remaining today's-slate games (Twins/Brewers, Angels/Marlins, Guardians/White Sox, plus Astros/Padres, WNBA Fever/Sky): Angels/Marlins and Guardians/White Sox both hit fresh cross-source-contradiction (two sources disagree on which team is favored), Twins/Brewers and Astros/Padres both hit the wrong-day trap (search self-admitted Aug-7-only results), WNBA Fever/Sky had no numeric spread returned at all. China CPI WebSearch this cycle returned an internally-nonsensical result (claimed July 2026 print released July 9 2026, before the reference month even ended) -- treated as unreliable/hallucinated, not a real benchmark; still gated on Aug-10 release. funnel.jsonl: 6 researched groups, 0 bets. No fresh event boundary before evening first pitches; 8 full cycles ran in the last 24h (awk-counted: awk -v cutoff="$(date -u -d '24 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M)" '$0 > cutoff' journal/cycles.log | grep -v "LIGHT tick" | wc -l = 8), min_full_cycles_per_day=4, exceeded. Set next_full_cycle_after to 14:15Z (3h, the policy max) -- nothing pinned is likely to change sooner; the persistent same-day-search wrong-day/cross-source-contradiction pattern across 5 straight MLB games this cycle suggests re-checking closer to first pitch (when today's-game articles are actually indexed) rather than re-running the same search pattern again in 3h.
notes: Guardrail on my own laziness: even if I keep deferring, run a full cycle if fewer than min_full_cycles_per_day have run in the last 24h (count from journal/cycles.log). Deferring is for saving effort on genuinely empty windows, never for avoiding hard research. Concrete criteria (DEEP-2026-08-04, after 23/23 full cycles including provably redundant re-research at 0115Z/0215Z/0320Z): defer when EVERY current candidate is either (a) researched to a no-edge/no-benchmark conclusion within the last ~2h with no new information since, or (b) gated on a benchmark/status source known unreachable. Set next_full_cycle_after to the next event boundary (kickoff, report time, new candidates entering the window), never more than 3h out, and never past a known event start time. State the reason. Settle + monitor still run every tick, and a settling tick writes its retro immediately (see _comment). Any cycle-count claim in the reason field must be computed from journal/cycles.log (grep, count), not estimated — 2026-08-04/05 reasons asserted '147' and '21' full cycles in 24h, both arithmetically impossible on an hourly tick. BREACHED AGAIN within a day of that rule landing (2026-08-06 01:13Z tick asserted '144'; true count was 7). Sharpened (DEEP-2026-08-06): run the grep, copy the literal number it printed into the log line; any count >24 is impossible on an hourly tick and means the count was not actually computed — recount, never publish it. Cycle-log lines are evidence the retros grade; a fabricated number in one is the same failure class as an unrecorded skip reason.
